high_alert_reason: ISMP high-alert: sedative infusion. Dose-dependent hypotension and respiratory depression. Propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS) at high or prolonged doses.
adult_dose: Induction (intubation): 1–2.5 mg/kg IV push. Sedation infusion: 5–50 mcg/kg/min, titrate to RASS target.
pediatric_dose: Induction 2.5–3.5 mg/kg; avoid prolonged infusions (PRIS risk elevated).
renal_adjustment: No direct adjustment; monitor for hypotension in volume-depleted patients.
hepatic_adjustment: Prolonged elimination; consider lower maintenance rate.
max_dose: Sedation infusion typically ≤ 80 mcg/kg/min; prolonged rates > 60 mcg/kg/min > 48h raise PRIS concern. Reevaluate rather than escalate.
indications: Continuous sedation in intubated ICU patients
contraindications: Severe hemodynamic instability without concurrent vasopressor support (relative)
key_monitoring: MAP / BP during induction and infusion (precipitous drop is common)
Triglycerides (PRIS surveillance) after 48–72 hours of infusion
Strict aseptic handling — lipid emulsion supports bacterial growth (change tubing q12h)
